subject: Priority lane + on-call escrow: clarifying takedown and credit triggers
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@brightline.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: 2028-05-28T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial terms question — priority lane + escrow concept

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the term sheet. A few things jumped out on our side as we review the priority-lane + on-call escrow proposal:

1) Takedown window language: you mention a 48h safe window before a severe takedown. Can you clarify whether that applies to customer-initiated takedowns for regulatory reasons, or only vendor-initiated decommissioning?

2) Escrow credits: the idea of allocating X on-call hours into an escrow account is interesting. How do credits burn if Brightline consumes rotated on-call (i.e., when we escalate to your engineers) versus when you proactively apply a hotfix?

3) Automated fallback & routing: if the priority lane is saturated, do requests automatically fall back to the regional shared pool? Any impact to cost/credits?

We want to avoid surprise billing or losing coverage mid-pilot. Can you send a short example scenario showing how credits flow and how a takedown/rollback would be executed?

Best,
Jared

--
Jared Cole
Director, Infrastructure
Brightline Inc
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@brightline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-28T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial terms question — priority lane + escrow concept

Hi Jared —

Thanks — good questions. Quick answers up front, followed by a short illustrative scenario attached.

1) Takedown window: the 48h window in the term sheet applies only to vendor-initiated decommissioning or planned capacity retirements (we call these ‘service lifecycle events’). Customer-initiated takedowns for compliance/DR are handled per your control-plane actions and are outside the vendor notice window. We can add explicit language to avoid ambiguity.

2) Escrow credits: credits are consumed in priority order: (a) customer-requested on-call escalation (consumes escrow hours first), (b) proactive vendor remediation (does not consume customer escrow unless remediation requires paid remote debugging beyond the SLA scope). We will include a short matrix in the term sheet.

3) Fallback routing: automatic fallback to the regional shared pool is supported. When fallback occurs, usage remains billable under your committed rate; priority-lane credits are not consumed unless you explicitly request a routed failover to reserved capacity. In plain terms: we won’t burn your escrow hours purely because the lane is saturated.

I attached a worked example and a diagram of the escrow lifecycle. If that looks right, Kimberly will follow up with a tightened term paragraph and a redline-friendly clause.

Regards,
Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@brightline.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-29T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial terms question — priority lane + escrow concept

Morning Jared —

Putting this into contract language now. A couple of precision points we think belong in the operational appendix (attached):

• Escrow reconciliation cadence: monthly statement + 30-day review; unused hours roll forward for pilot only (6-month cap)
• Credit burn logic: we’ll enumerate the exact triggers (customer escalation, vendor-initiated emergency patch, region failover) and map each to whether escrow or vendor labor is billed.
• Emergency takedown: define a 4-step cadence (notification, approval window, mitigation plan, post-mortem). Vendor-initiated takedowns will include a 72‑hour remediation guarantee or a financial credit tied to the uptime band.

Attached: PriorityLane_Termsheet_v1.pdf and a proposed OncallEscrow_Workflow.drawio we’ll insert into the SOW. Jord, can you confirm the SLA-credit matrix values we discussed yesterday (esp. the 99.95 vs 99.9 tradeoff)?

Thanks — I’ll send a redline by end of day after Jared confirms the two bullets above.

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Cole <jared.cole@brightline.com>
Date: 2028-05-29T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial terms question — priority lane + escrow concept

Hi all —

Confirming the SLA-credit matrix (summary):
• 99.95% uptime: base price + priority-lane retainer, credit = 5% monthly invoice for <99.95 but >=99.9
• 99.9% uptime: lower retainer, credit = 10% monthly invoice for <99.9 but >=99.5
• <99.5%: escalated remediation + pro-rata refund & extended priority hours at no charge until remediation completes

Important callout: if Brightline exercises an emergency takedown that results in degraded availability, we will not apply standard SLA credits for vendor-controlled failures; credits only apply where Redwood is the root cause. We typically document a short cause taxonomy to make adjudication faster.

Also added a row for on-call escrow consumption: proactive remediation (no credit consumption) vs reactive on-call (consumes escrow hours first, then billable if escrow exhausted). I attached the SLA-credit-matrix.xlsx.

Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Escalations, Redwood Inference
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@brightline.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: 2028-05-30T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial terms question — priority lane + escrow concept

Thanks — that clears up most items. A few follow-ups before we sign the pilot SOW: 

1) Can you add a simple example in the SOW: "customer consumes 10 escrow hours for escalations in month 1; vendor applies a proactive remediation in month 2 that does not burn escrow; month 3 has a regional outage that is vendor-caused, triggering a 5% invoice credit" — helps procurement approve.

2) We need explicit wording around legal hold / data retention during takedown windows. Who owns snapshots taken by Brightline, and will Redwood preserve any logs for 120 days by default?

3) Final ask: can we get a one-page executive summary that maps the three uptime bands to price delta (e.g., +15% for 99.95 vs 99.9) for the procurement team? If you can send that as a PDF, procurement will greenlight the pilot this week.

If you can return the redline + one-pager by EOD Thursday (June 1 PT), I’ll push it through Brightline legal.

Appreciate the speed — Jared

--
Jared Cole
Director, Infrastructure
Brightline Inc
